cohort: Newborns transported to a Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU) in Northeast Italy between January 1, 2018 and December 31, 2019
finding: Infants with birth weight ≤2500 grams had a higher incidence of cesarean birth, longer infant stabilization time, longer NICU stay, and received more intravenous therapy and invasive ventilation compared to infants with birth weight >2500 grams.
mod_finding: For newborns weighing >2500 grams, there was a low incidence of cesarean birth compared to vaginal delivery, while the percentages were reversed in the group of infants ≤2500 grams.
